findings.message: This Dependabot configuration does not set a cooldown period. Newly published packages can be malicious or unstable. Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-version-updates/configuration-options-for-the-dependabot.yml-file#cooldown
findings.reason: Build dependency/lifecycle policy deserves review, but these settings alone are not proof of compromise. Check needed install scripts and locally installed Playwright before disabling scripts or changing npx/cooldown behavior.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/master_glosify.yml:97-119; package locks; dependabot.yml
findings.assessment_depth: follow-up required; not confirmed or dismissed

findings.message: Affected versions of sharp are vulnerable to Divide By Zero / Heap-based Buffer Overflow / Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. sharp bundles a vulnerable version of the native libheif library, inheriting two critical memory-safety flaws in derived-item (`iden`) and auxiliary-item (`auxl`) handling: a heap buffer overflow in `scale_nearest_neighbor()` where duplicate alpha planes let a 10/12-bit sample be written into an 8-bit plane allocation with an attacker-controlled overflow size and contents (CVE-2026-84383), and a class of out-of-bounds reads and writes across roughly a dozen pixel-plane consumers that assume a `HeifPixelImage` logical geometry matching every channel plane it holds (GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545, for which a working code-execution exploit was confirmed). Decoding a crafted AVIF or HEIF image can therefore corrupt the heap and lead to remote code execution. Because sharp selects the libvips loader by sniffing the input bytes, no call site can be shown to be safe: `sharp(untrustedBuffer)` reaches the libheif loader exactly as `sharp("photo.avif")` does, and even a metadata-only `.metadata()` call parses the container. Upgrade to sharp 0.35.4 or later, which bundles libheif 1.23.2; if you rely on a globally-installed libvips, upgrade that libheif to 1.23.2. Blocking the HEIF-family loader with `sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadHeif"] })` is the only workaround that prevents the vulnerable decode path from being reached; running a `node` binary compiled as a Position Independent Executable merely blunts escalation to code execution and does not stop the heap corruption, and the official Node.js builds are not PIE. The heap corruption itself is platform-independent; the advisory documents escalation to remote code execution on glibc-based Linux hosts running a non-PIE `node` binary, so a finding on macOS or musl still represents an exploitable memory-safety bug.

findings.message: Affected versions of undici are vulnerable to Improper Certificate Validation. undici's `BalancedPool` deep-clones its constructor options with a JSON round-trip before passing them to its upstream pools, so function values in the `connect` or `tls` options (such as a `checkServerIdentity` callback or a custom connector) are silently dropped. Custom TLS certificate verification never runs, and certificates that pass Node's default checks are accepted, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks against applications that rely on certificate pinning or custom identity checks.

findings.message: Promises must be awaited, end with a call to .catch, end with a call to .then with a rejection handler or be explicitly marked as ignored with the `void` operator.
findings.reason: Inspected awaited I/O is handled inside the called function (try/catch or Promise.allSettled), including rendering, translation, voice catalog and assistant loading. The absent caller .catch alone does not prove an unhandled expected failure. This does not guarantee arbitrary programming errors cannot reject.
